x: Pearson scored in all of our winning teams, whilst Tommy Clinton and Dick Tobin graduated from the "B" team in the South of the Thames "Junior" to the winning team in the National.
Owing to the forward running of Dick Tobin 5, and Tom Clinton 7, our "B" team gained second awards, and our congratulations go to Charlie Smart and John Weames, who completed the "B" team.

Pearson and Tom Clinton, came along together and the team race was assured. Bert Mitchell and Tom Morrell completed our scoring six and we once again became the proud holders of the "Dewar" Shield, which is awarded to the winning club.

Tom Clinton ran very well to hand over in second place and George Hoath, running for our "B" team, was in third place. Both our "C" and "D" teams were also well up and we were the only club to field and, what is more important, close in four complete teams.

Wynyard was third in the 440 and Tom Clinton ran in good style to win the 2 miles event. We had to make up a scratch team for the medley relay, but even so Derrick Burfitt almost caught Anzola of T.V.H. over the final stage.
Tom Morrell did manage a fourth place in the latter event, and in the 2 miles Tom Clinton was second, with Frank Abberton third, in 9 min. 53 secs.

I am not forgetting such as Dick Tobin, Geoff Pearson, Tom Clinton and Tom Carter, who were all members of our last winning “ National ” team; also Stan Eales, who backed up our teams so well last season; but these members cannot carry on for ever, and it is to the newer members that we look to to c…

Les Grimshaw turned out with his leg strapped up and won the 100 yards for us, and Syd Jarlett won the 880 yards in quite his old style. Len Herbert captured the 1 mile with his brother Eric in fourth place, and Les Stokell won the 2 miles with Tom Clinton second.

Cope a new member introduced by George Weston, showed his worth by winning the 880 yards in 2 mins. 1.6 secs. Our leading men in the 2 miles race were Archie Bedford, Frank Abberton and Tom Clinton, but W.
Blowfield, second, and Tommy Clinton, fifth, ran exceptionally well and were both chosen for Middlesex in the Inter Counties C.C.
Gosney of Eastleigh beat Olney the local "crack" in the individual race, but our lads packed well with Tom Clinton 4th, Dick Towndrow 5th, Ted Stimpson 6th and Frank Abberton 7th.

Tom Clinton ran a good leg and handed over to George Lucas at Merstham in sixth place. George started with supreme confidence on his 4½ miles jaunt up Redhill and along the switchback to the Prince Albert where he handed over in second place, clocking 22 mins. 36 secs., only 4 secs. slower running t…
Tom Clinton has also done very well and he won the Portsmouth A.C. 10 miles race on March 29th when we finished second in the team race with Tom Carter 7th and Dick Tobin 11th completing our team.

Newcomers to the team were Tom Clinton, Ken Stimpson, Martin Williamson and Eddie Short. Twenty-five clubs competed in 1949 and we accomplished our second hat-trick of wins, thus achieving more wins in the nineteen races held than any other club.
But Sutton still had five in before our 5th man (Tom Carter 41st) and then praise be, Tommy Clinton came along in 57th place to complete our scoring six, while Sutton's 6th man finished 65th!

Africa; brother Alec has also been wounded but has returned to his unit---Arthur Beales is missing from air operations over Germany---Tommy Clinton (Irish Guards) writes from hospital that he was wounded just before last Christmas whilst on a landing trip.

Len Herbert had run well throughout as had Ted Stimpson, now getting back to his pre-war form, and with Frank Abberton also making a last lap effort, and Tom Carter and Tommy Clinton coming along well we found to our satisfaction that we had beaten Sutton Harriers, the holders, to record our fourth National victory.

Geoff was one of that rare breed of Belgravian who had sampled team success at the highest level, being fourth scorer, in 21st position, in our winning National Cross Country team at Leamington Spa in 1946. The others in the winning team that day were Len Herbert (5th), Dave Main (11th), Tom Carter (13th), 21 T.G.
